title: The design rules say how a menu row is capitalised
goal: The video mocks write menu rows in sentence case (Apply to every cut, Reset to defaults) and the app writes them in Mac title case (Apply to Every Cut, Reset to Defaults). Nothing in the design rules says which wins, so every task that adds a menu row picks one, explains itself in its audit, and the user reads the same departure again and again. Settle it once in the rules.
notes: Recurring in audits across four tasks in three days: the-dock-headers-match-the-mock-small-caps-title (Copy Look vs the mock's Copy properties), the-properties-menu-puts-a-clip-back-the-way-it (queue/audits/2026-09-27-properties-reset-to-defaults.json: 'Items are Title Case like every other menu in the app'), one-step-puts-a-transition-on-every-cut (queue/audits/2026-09-27-transition-on-every-cut.json: 'Menu rows are in macOS title case ... the mock writes sentence case'), one-key-puts-the-usual-transition-on-the-cut-at. grep of UX-PATTERNS.md and AGENTS.md finds no casing rule.
acceptance: docs/design/mocks/shared/UX-PATTERNS.md says in one rule how a menu row, a menu heading and a button label are capitalised, and whether the mock's casing or the Mac's wins
If the rule departs from the mocks, a decision card put it to the user first, since mocks are the floor
Every menu row the app shows in Next follows the rule, checked by a test over the menu titles the app registers

log.note: Surveyed: every mock page writes menu rows in sentence case (app-shell: Copy properties, Reset to style; agent pages: Group selection, Make component). The app's menu rows are uniformly Mac title case: a rough scan of menu and contextMenu sources found 127 title-case rows, 0 sentence-case rows; the only sentence-case strings were panel buttons/labels (MotionListInspector: 'Draw a curve...', 'Use this curve'; 'Between the keys' is a section label). macOS injects title-case rows (Select All, Enter Full Screen) the app cannot reword. UX-PATTERNS §4/§7 have no casing rule. Since the recommended rule (title case) departs from the mocks, acceptance item 2 requires a card first: opened the-design-rules-say-how-a-menu-row-is-capitalis-how-should-a-menu-row-and-a-butt with brief. Nothing further is decidable before the answer: the rule text and the test over registered menu titles both depend on which style wins.

The recommended rule (Mac title case) departs from the mocks, so the user decides first: card the-design-rules-say-how-a-menu-row-is-capitalis-how-should-a-menu-row-and-a-butt. Rule text and the menu-title test follow the answer.
decision "How should a menu row and a button be capitalised: Apply to Every Cut (the Mac) or Apply to every cut (the mocks)?" resolved: The Mac way: Title Case
